hook: "Fake it till you make it" doesn't build social confidence. Here's what it actually builds.
body:
**"Fake it till you make it" doesn't build social confidence. It builds a more elaborate performance — and a growing private suspicion that the real you still isn't enough.**

Here's the problem with performing confidence. The performance requires monitoring. You have to track whether you're pulling it off, adjust when it slips, maintain the gap between how you feel and how you're presenting. That gap doesn't close over time. It gets more familiar. You get better at maintaining it. But it's still a gap.

And because nothing in that process requires you to update your actual nervous system baseline, the anxiety underneath doesn't go anywhere. It just gets a better costume.

Real social confidence — the kind that travels with you regardless of how the room is going — doesn't come from performing security until it becomes habit. It comes from experiences that actually update your body's belief about whether social situations are safe.

Small moments of genuine connection. Conversations where you were yourself and it went well. Rooms where you didn't disappear and nothing terrible happened. These are the inputs that shift the baseline. Not the performance, but the evidence.

The goal isn't to fake security. It's to accumulate enough real evidence that your system starts to genuinely believe it.

More in my bio.
